PINTAR production application deployment — request

Editing this file launches the Vercel deployment workflow; ordinary commits on
the deployment branch do nothing. Each entry records one attempt.

release:  46fd4452ebc7b861abb5cb9b1963178088b978a7
target:   Vercel project "pintar40" (scope yazidmanan-2409)

auth:     HELD. Not configured until Second Eye clears the deployment.
why:      the assertion worked: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY is genuinely
          absent from Vercel production. Its `vercel env add` returned success
          and stored nothing, while the variables written seconds either side
          of it are present. A write that can fail silently is not a write, so
          environment values now go through the Vercel API, which upserts and
          reports its failures. No build was spent on the incomplete set.

          Previously: ATTEMPT 007 GOT THE APPLICATION RUNNING. Declaring framework=nextjs
          turned the platform 404 into a 500: the app is deployed, routed and
          executing, and pintar40.vercel.app routes now too. The deployment
          carries four function outputs where it previously carried none.

          A 500 is an application error, and the deployment's build env lists
          every variable except NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY -- which
          publicSupabaseAnonKey() throws without, on a page that builds a
          Supabase client while rendering. Writing an environment value is not
          the same as it being there, so the set is now read back from Vercel
          and asserted before a build is spent on it.

          Previously: the custom domain proved the real state. It is NOT behind SSO --
          the all_except_custom_domains exemption works -- and it answered a
          platform 404 NOT_FOUND with zero redirects, from iad1. The
          *.vercel.app hosts answer 302 to vercel.com/sso-api, so SSO had been
          masking this the whole time: the application has never served a page
          to anyone, through any hostname, in any attempt.

          The project was created by `vercel project add` and carried
          framework: null, buildCommand: null, outputDirectory: null. The
          deployment held one lambda with entrypoint "." and no output. That
          is a Next.js application Vercel was never told was Next.js. This
          attempt declares the framework, then rebuilds and redeploys.
